edbDesc: Aircraft may be affected by a number of ground effects, or aerodynamic effects due to a flying body's proximity to the ground.
title: Ground effect
description: A wing flying closer to the ground or water than about half its span gets extra lift and less drag, because the surface stops air from escaping downward and swirling round the wingtips. Carl Wieselsberger measured it in 1922; pilots feel it as a 'float' just before touchdown.
effect: a wing close to the ground gets more lift and less drag
usedIn: Soviet ekranoplans such as the 'Caspian Sea Monster'
strength: Flying at a tenth of its span above the surface, a wing loses roughly half its induced drag, which is why ekranoplans could carry heavy loads on little fuel.
pickWhy: A specific aerodynamic effect with real vehicles built on it; not in the deck.
